Operation Juno.fact: Between 10 and 12 June Marschall sortied with Gneisenau, Admiral Hipper and the destroyers; due to a lack of air reconnaissance and the presence of the British fleet he returned to Trondheim.

Operation Juno.subject: Applied Sciences
Operation Juno.question: On 13 June, 15 Skua bombers of the _____, from Ark Royal, attacked Scharnhorst in harbour
Operation Juno.fact: On 13 June, 15 Skua bombers of the Fleet Air Arm, from Ark Royal, attacked Scharnhorst in harbour.

Operation Juno.subject: Applied Sciences
Operation Juno.question: One dud bomb struck her for the loss of eight _____
Operation Juno.fact: One dud bomb struck her for the loss of eight Skuas.

Operation Juno.subject: Applied Sciences
Operation Juno.question: After emergency repairs in _____ of the torpedo damage, Scharnhorst departed for Germany escorted by the four destroyers, reaching Kiel on 23 June to go into dry dock
Operation Juno.fact: Between 10 and 12 June Marschall sortied with Gneisenau, Admiral Hipper and the destroyers; due to a lack of air reconnaissance and the presence of the British fleet he returned to Trondheim. After emergency repairs in Trondheim of the torpedo damage, Scharnhorst departed for Germany escorted by the four destroyers, reaching Kiel on 23 June to go into dry dock.

Operation Juno.subject: Applied Sciences
Operation Juno.question: To cover the withdrawal of _____, Marschall sortied with Gneisenau and Admiral Hipper from Trondheim on 20 June but Gneisenau was torpedoed and damaged in the bows by the British submarine HMS Clyde
Operation Juno.fact: On 13 June, 15 Skua bombers of the Fleet Air Arm, from Ark Royal, attacked Scharnhorst in harbour. After emergency repairs in Trondheim of the torpedo damage, Scharnhorst departed for Germany escorted by the four destroyers, reaching Kiel on 23 June to go into dry dock.

Operation Juno.subject: Applied Sciences
Operation Juno.question: Scharnhorst and _____ remained under repair until the end of 1940
Operation Juno.fact: To cover the withdrawal, Marschall sortied with Gneisenau and Admiral Hipper from Trondheim on 20 June but Gneisenau was torpedoed by HMS Clyde. Scharnhorst and Gneisenau remained under repair until the end of 1940.
